intro: Bass, walleye and striped bass are what anglers travel here for. The Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission manages the lake under the ordinary statewide rules.
fine: This is a guide, not the law. Seasons and limits change every year, so check the Commission's current summary book before you keep a fish.

items.note: Smallmouth and largemouth bass, walleye, chain pickerel, yellow perch, striped bass, brown trout, channel catfish and panfish. The Commission's 2021 netting survey also turned up northern pike, black crappie, bluegill and rock bass.
items.link: Fish and Boat Commission lake page

items.note: Striped bass, walleye and brown trout go in as fingerlings. Most of the lake's fish sustain themselves; channel catfish have reproduced on their own since 2001. The lake is also where the Commission collects its walleye brood stock.

sections.title: Rules in brief (2026)
sections.text: No special rules for this lake; statewide inland limits apply. A fishing licence is required from age 16.

items.note: Open all year. 20 inch minimum, 2 a day combined.
January 1 to March 14 and May 2 to December 31. 15 inch minimum, 6 a day.
January 1 to April 10 and October 1 to December 31: 15 inch minimum, 4 a day. April 11 to June 12: catch and release only. June 13 to September 30: 12 inch minimum, 6 a day.
Pickerel 18 inch minimum, 4 a day. Northern pike 24 inch minimum, 2 a day.
Open all year, no minimum size, 50 a day combined.
Pennsylvania advises no more than one meal a month of walleye from this lake, because of mercury.
Seasons, sizes and limits for the current year.

Fish and Boat Commission ramp off Route 590, half a mile from Route 6. Free to launch, with an accessible fishing pier and room for about 48 trailers. The docks came out in late September 2026 for the drawdown and are due back in late March 2027.
113 Ammon Drive, Hawley. Run for the dam's owner, Brookfield; launch fee, waived for campers.
431 Lakeshore Drive, Lakeville. Launch fee, waived for campers.
155 Burns Hill Road, Greentown. Launch fee, waived for campers; accessible fishing pier.
153 Ledgedale Road, Greentown. Launch fee, waived for campers.
Shoreline fishing access near Routes 6 and 507.
About two miles of shoreline to fish, with parking on Route 590.
Accessible piers at Mangan Cove and Ironwood Point.
The visitors center at 2512 Route 6 lends rods and tackle free.
Fishing is not allowed in the Beech House Creek Wildlife Refuge.
25 mph from sunset to sunrise. 45 mph by day on weekends and holidays from the Saturday before Memorial Day through Labor Day. No horsepower limit.
Wallenpaupack Creek; about 1,000 feet below Ledgedale Bridge; within about 600 feet of the dam; and between Cairns Island and the Pike County shore.

The Commission says ice here is not officially monitored by any authority, and people have gone through. Wear a life jacket, carry ice awls, test with an ice staff as you go, and never go alone. Five lines at most while ice fishing.
Stocked in Pike County from just above Middle Creek to the mouth, and in Wayne County below the Dyberry Creek confluence.
Stocked from the Mountain Cobb Road bridge to the Forks Road bridge. A 1.74 mile trophy trout stretch, artificial lures only, runs down to Callapoose Road.
Jones Creek from the Mountain Cobb Road bridge to its mouth; Decker Brook from the second Route 6 bridge down to the state game lands line.
30 Welwood Avenue, Hawley.
